articles.title: Sobering Outcomes after Two-Stage Revision for Periprosthetic Joint Infection Among Patients Who Have Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty Components.
articles.authors: Ball JR, Palmer RC, Telang SS, Aron A, Bruce D, Jones-Lopez EC, et al.
articles.population: Patients treated with complete removal of infected revision total knee replacement components at a tertiary academic centre
articles.outcomes: Reoperation rates, reinfection, intensive care admission, readmission within 90 days, amputation, and 10-year survivorship free from reoperation and reinfection
articles.take_home: Removing an infected revision knee replacement is associated with significant complications, with only about 35% of patients free from further surgery at 10 years and one in three patients who had a new implant placed needing another operation, often due to recurrent infection. Five patients required amputation of the leg.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Increased Lengths of Stay After Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Single Institution Retrospective Review.
articles.authors: Brito M, Heo KY, Rieger E, Paige D, Syed O, Chandrashekar A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty at an orthopaedic specialty hospital
articles.outcomes: Length of stay and timing of discharge following total hip arthroplasty; factors associated with later-day discharge
articles.take_home: Most patients (93.5%) were discharged on the same day as surgery. Patients were more likely to stay longer if they had a lower RAPT score, had surgery later in the day, or had a longer operation, suggesting that preoperative planning using these factors could help hospitals plan discharges better.

articles.title: Isolated lateral compartment cartilage changes on preoperative magnetic resonance imaging should not automatically preclude medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty: A cohort study of 100 magnetic resonance imaging scans.
articles.authors: Bunyoz KI, Troelsen A, Jackson W, Bottomley N, Alvand A, Price A
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial unicompartmental knee replacement with preoperative MRI scans
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery for any cause at mean 9.6 years follow-up; cumulative revision incidence at 10 years
articles.take_home: Finding cartilage damage in the outer part of the knee on MRI before medial unicompartmental knee replacement should not automatically stop patients having the operation. Patients with these changes had a similar or lower revision rate compared to those without.

articles.title: Limited predictive value of preseason isokinetic strength testing for noncontact lower extremity injuries in elite female football players: A 5-year prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Seiler J, Haas A, Gnadinger D, Bode G, Rosa M, Prill R, et al.
articles.population: Professional and elite youth female football players (under 20 and under 17)
articles.outcomes: Noncontact lower extremity injuries including ACL, meniscus, collateral ligament, ankle and muscle injuries (70 injuries recorded total)
articles.take_home: Preseason strength testing alone is not reliable for predicting injuries in female footballers, although a higher hamstring-to-quadriceps ratio showed modest protection. Strength testing should be combined with other assessment methods rather than used as a standalone screening tool.

articles.title: Higher prearthritic activity is associated with higher long-term activity after medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Cerasoli T, Tabanelli B, Scagnol D, Di Maio L, Neri MP, Rinaldi VG, et al.
articles.population: Patients who had medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Sport participation and activity level at long-term follow-up (mean 116 months), measured using Tegner Activity Scale
articles.take_home: Most people returned to sport after this type of knee replacement, with activity levels nearly returning to pre-arthritis levels. People who were more active before developing arthritis tended to be more active after their knee replacement.

articles.title: Static Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee phenotypes are associated with distinct dynamic knee kinematics in advanced knee osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Tian D, Wang H, Chen Z, Zhang J, Yao S, Zhang W, et al.
articles.population: Patients with advanced knee osteoarthritis awaiting total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 292 knees from 160 patients (mean age 65 years, 67.5% women)
articles.outcomes: Knee motion during walking including flexion-extension, rotation, side-to-side movement and forward-backward translation for different knee alignment types
articles.take_home: Different types of knee alignment, measured on standing X-rays, show distinct patterns of movement when walking in patients with severe knee osteoarthritis. Measuring how knees actually move during walking could provide useful additional information alongside static alignment measurements before knee replacement surgery.

articles.title: Beyond clinical grading: rethinking arthrogenic muscle inhibition after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Qu X, Tang X, Yang D, Chen B
articles.population: Patients after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Arthrogenic muscle inhibition assessed by clinical SANTI classification and mechanistic measures including voluntary activation and transcranial magnetic stimulation
articles.take_home: Clinical grading systems like SANTI are useful for routine screening of muscle activation problems after knee ligament surgery, but they should not be confused with understanding the actual mechanisms causing these problems. A full assessment needs additional tests of muscle activation and should consider pain during movement, not just pain ratings alone.

articles.title: A comparative study of machine learning based automatic diagnosis approaches to diagnose knee osteoarthritis from radiographs.
articles.authors: Chandra S, Priyadarshini, Pathak V
articles.study_type: Systematic review of machine learning diagnostic approaches
articles.population: Middle-aged and elderly people with knee osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of machine learning methods for detecting and grading knee osteoarthritis from X-rays
articles.take_home: This review examined how artificial intelligence systems can automatically detect and grade knee osteoarthritis from X-rays more consistently than human observers, but challenges remain in making these systems work reliably in everyday clinical practice.

articles.title: Optimizing perioperative intravenous corticosteroid dosing for postoperative outcomes in total joint arthroplasty: a network meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Kao PE, Ker A, Hsu CW, Shouh Hsu AH, Wu CT, Lin PC, et al.
articles.study_type: Network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty or total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 2,936 participants across 27 randomised controlled trials (25 included in analysis)
articles.outcomes: 24-hour postoperative pain at rest and during movement; rescue antiemetic use
articles.take_home: Low-dose intravenous steroids reduce postoperative pain and nausea after hip or knee replacement surgery, with higher doses potentially offering extra pain relief in certain situations. Most benefits were achieved with lower steroid doses rather than very high doses.

articles.title: Tibial migration of a novel cementless total knee arthroplasty : a multicentre radiostereometric analysis study.
articles.authors: Naudie DDR, Lanting BA, Bohm E, Teeter M, Righolt C, Turgeon TR, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Tibial baseplate migration measured by maximum total point motion at 6, 12 and 24 months; patient-reported outcome measures including Oxford Knee Score, Forgotten Joint Score and EuroQol five-dimension questionnaire
articles.take_home: A new cementless knee implant baseplate showed stable fixation over two years with minimal movement that stayed below levels suggesting future loosening problems. Patients reported good functional improvements and high satisfaction with the implant.

articles.title: Comparable functional outcomes after total hip arthroplasty in patients with and without prior ipsilateral hip arthroscopy: A comparative cohort study.
articles.authors: Krautter J, Feil S, Thorey F
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty, with and without prior hip arthroscopy on the same side
articles.sample_size: 546 patients (89 with prior arthroscopy, 457 with primary arthroplasty)
articles.outcomes: Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS), Harris Hip Score, Oxford Hip Score, Visual Analogue Scale, complication rates and revision rates
articles.take_home: Patients who had hip arthroscopy before hip replacement achieved similar functional improvements and outcomes compared to those having primary hip replacement. Having previous arthroscopy on the same side is unlikely to compromise the functional result of subsequent hip replacement surgery.

articles.title: Preserved anterolateral ligament graft continuity on MRI and lower knee laxity after ACL graft failure than before index combined ACL-ALL reconstruction: A retrospective case series.
articles.authors: Leao RV, Takamune DM, da Silva AGM, Camerin GR, Ariel de Lima D, Helito CP
articles.population: Patients who experienced ACL graft failure after combined ACL-ALL reconstruction
articles.outcomes: ALL graft continuity on MRI, anteroposterior knee laxity (anterior tibial translation), rotational laxity (pivot-shift grade)
articles.take_home: After the main ACL graft failed, the ALL graft remained intact in all patients and knee laxity was actually lower than before the original surgery. Doctors should be cautious when examining these patients because the knee may feel more stable than expected even though the main ACL graft has failed.

articles.title: No difference in short-term revision risk between robot-assisted total knee arthroplasty and conventional techniques: An analysis of 79,115 total knee arthroplasties in the Dutch arthroplasty register.
articles.authors: Vink MC, Vossen RJM, Peters RM, Spekenbrink-Spooren A, Rijk PC, Jutte PC, et al.
articles.study_type: Registry analysis using competing risk and multivariable Cox regression
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty for end-stage knee osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Revision risk at 2 years follow-up; implant survival; reasons for revision
articles.take_home: Robot-assisted and conventional knee replacement surgery had similar revision rates at 2 years, with no meaningful difference in safety or outcomes. Both techniques showed low overall revision rates, though longer follow-up is needed to assess performance beyond the short term.

articles.title: Injectable hydrogel filled into porous scaffolds combined with ultrasound-controlled drug release.
articles.authors: Xu Y, Zhao P, Lin Q, Zhang H, Shen L, Ye Y, et al.
articles.population: Rats with carrageenan-induced arthritis
articles.outcomes: Knee swelling, pain sensitivity, drug release rates, cell compatibility
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a combination of injectable hydrogel and 3D-printed scaffolds that can deliver anti-inflammatory medication on demand using ultrasound. In arthritic rats, this treatment reduced knee swelling and improved pain relief compared to untreated animals.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of intra-articular disease-modifying osteoarthritis drugs (DMOADs) for knee osteoarthritis: a Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.authors: Wong K, Low WX, Shafiei A, Al Hosni R, Liew I
articles.study_type: Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Patients with knee osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2-3)
articles.outcomes: Cartilage thickness, pain improvement, function, and adverse events
articles.take_home: None of the four disease-modifying drugs tested (Sprifermin, Lorecivivint, SB-061, and LNA043) showed clear benefits for slowing knee osteoarthritis or reducing pain and disability compared to placebo. Better treatments and more rigorous studies are needed.

articles.title: Radiological pattern of hip osteoarthritis is associated with one-year patient-reported outcomes but not long-term mortality or revision after total hip arthroplasty : a retrospective case series.
articles.authors: McCann CJ, Clement ND, Bayram JM, Leitch G, Scott CEH
articles.population: Patients with primary hip osteoarthritis undergoing total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Oxford Hip Score and EQ-5D-3L quality of life scores at one year; long-term mortality and revision rates over mean 12.3 years follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients with hypertrophic hip osteoarthritis had greater functional improvement one year after hip replacement surgery compared to those with atrophic osteoarthritis, but the type of osteoarthritis did not affect long-term survival or need for revision surgery.

articles.title: Patients Undergoing Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty for Stiffness Have Similar Perioperative Pain Scores and Postoperative Opioid Consumption Compared to Patients Undergoing Revisions for Other Aseptic Indications.
articles.authors: Shin J, Driscoll DA, Selkridge I, Somerby H, Chalmers BP, Lee GC, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee replacement for stiffness or aseptic loosening/instability
articles.outcomes: Postoperative pain scores at six weeks, 90-day opioid use, duration of opioid use, morphine milligram equivalents consumed, and number of opioid refills
articles.take_home: Patients having revision knee replacement for stiffness needed similar amounts of painkiller and reported similar pain levels as those having revision surgery for other reasons, despite more of them having used painkillers before their operation. However, these results should be treated cautiously due to lower response rates in the stiffness group.

articles.title: The mechanism of injury's role in jump landing mechanics after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Hopper HM, Bruce-Leicht AS, Hart JM, Thompson XD
articles.population: Patients who had undergone primary isolated uncomplicated ACL reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Landing Error Scoring System (LESS) score, strength, and patient-reported outcomes at 8 months post-surgery
articles.take_home: Whether an ACL injury happened through contact or noncontact did not affect how patients landed and performed jumping movements after surgery. Many patients still had landing errors, suggesting that working on landing mechanics remains important throughout rehabilitation.

articles.title: Formal consensus on fast-track hip and knee arthroplasty: ESSKA/EKA, EHS and APAS recommendations for optimised recovery pathways in joint replacement surgeries.
articles.authors: Totlis T, Kort N, Kort R, Budhiparama NC, Carulli C, Clarius M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip and knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 106 expert panellists across steering, rating and peer review groups
articles.outcomes: 63 consensus statements on perioperative care across preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative phases; 39 statements graded as high or moderate evidence; mean agreement scores 7.7 to 8.9
articles.take_home: International experts agree that structured fast-track or enhanced recovery programmes for hip and knee replacement can reduce complications, improve pain control, shorten hospital stays and increase patient satisfaction. The recommendations provide a practical framework to guide consistent, safe care and support early mobilisation and discharge.

articles.title: Current concepts in isolated and combined injuries of the medial collateral ligament complex-Part I: Anatomy, biomechanics, clinical and radiological examination of the medial collateral ligament of the knee.
articles.authors: Runer A, Amis A, Smigielski R, Herbst E, Kittl C, Wierer G, et al.
articles.population: Patients with medial collateral ligament injuries or combined anterior cruciate ligament and medial collateral ligament injuries
articles.outcomes: Anatomy, biomechanics, clinical examination findings and radiological assessment of medial collateral ligament complex injuries
articles.take_home: This review explains how different parts of the medial collateral ligament complex work together to stabilise the knee and provides guidance on how to properly examine and diagnose these injuries using clinical tests and imaging.

articles.title: ACL injury mechanism in elite and recreational handball players.
articles.authors: Mayntzhusen TW, Barfod KW, Andersen FF, Holmich P, Kaldau NC
articles.population: Handball players with ACL injuries identified from Danish National Patient Register
articles.sample_size: 4540 handball players with ACL injuries (from 40,691 total respondents)
articles.outcomes: ACL injury mechanism, contact type, activity during injury, player position, sex and age differences
articles.take_home: Most ACL injuries in handball happen without contact during pivoting movements or single-leg landings, usually when players have the ball and are feinting or shooting in the opponent's half of the court. Back-line players and female players had higher injury rates, with females experiencing more non-contact injuries.

articles.title: Increased medial posterior tibial slope is associated with greater postoperative anterior tibial translation over time after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Paul S, Ghandour M, Jacquet C, Kley K, Sammartino F, Ollivier M
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with semitendinosus autograft
articles.outcomes: Medial posterior tibial slope and anterior tibial translation measured on radiographs at 2 months, 1 year and 2 years postoperatively
articles.take_home: A steeper angle of the tibial bone (medial posterior tibial slope) was weakly associated with greater forward movement of the tibia after ACL surgery over 2 years, but this effect was reduced if patients also had a lateral extra-articular tenodesis procedure. Older age and cartilage damage in the middle of the knee were associated with more instability early after surgery.

articles.title: Reimplantation in 2-Stage Exchange: Breaking the Dogma of the 2-Week Antibiotic Holiday.
articles.authors: Ascione T, Balato G, Pagliano P, Parvizi J
articles.population: Patients with periprosthetic joint infection undergoing 2-stage exchange revision
articles.outcomes: Timing of reimplantation, infection resolution, cure rates, treatment duration
articles.take_home: Current evidence does not support stopping antibiotics before reimplantation in infected joint replacements. Continuing antibiotics throughout treatment may lead to shorter overall treatment duration and better cure rates, especially in patients with weakened immune systems.

articles.title: A Novel Mini-Prosthesis with a Nano-Multilayer Film-Coated Surface and 3D-Printed Porous Stem for Focal Cartilage Lesions: In Vivo Performance in a Porcine Model.
articles.authors: Shang G, Mu Y, Wang K, Guo Z, Li Z, Li J
articles.population: Bama pigs with surgically created focal cartilage lesions of the knee
articles.sample_size: 25 pigs (50 knees total) in 5 treatment groups
articles.outcomes: Implant safety, bone integration, cartilage damage to surrounding joint surfaces, cartilage gene expression, inflammatory markers, and radiographic findings at 24 weeks
articles.take_home: A new mini-prosthesis with a special nano-coated surface and 3D-printed stem showed better bone integration and caused less damage to surrounding cartilage compared to a standard metal prosthesis or microfracture repair in this animal study. The new design was safe and well-tolerated, suggesting it may be useful for treating focal knee cartilage damage in patients.

articles.title: Quantifying the Age-Dependent Risk of Periprosthetic Femoral Fracture Following Cementless Total Hip Arthroplasty: An Analysis using Age as a Continuous Variable.
articles.authors: Griffith K, Telang SS, Palmer RC, Liu K, Dobitsch A, Lieberman JR, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective database analysis using multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline modelling
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary cementless total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Incidence of periprosthetic femoral fracture within 90 days after surgery
articles.take_home: The risk of fracture around the hip implant increases with age, with a noticeable rise beyond 71 years in women and 72 years in men. By age 80, the fracture risk is substantially higher than at the identified threshold ages.

articles.title: Biological Age Acceleration Predicts Functional Decline and Surgical Risk in Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Watanabe N, Yagi M, Naito Y, Ohtani S, Fujita R
articles.population: Adults with osteoarthritis undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Gait speed, muscle mass, and perioperative complications including deep vein thrombosis
articles.take_home: Biological age (calculated from blood tests) was better at predicting how well people recovered and what complications they had after knee surgery than their actual age. Smoking and heavy drinking were linked to faster biological ageing.

articles.title: Peripheral Artery Disease Is Associated With Increased Complications Following Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Tummala S, Sontam TR, Thota DR, Valencia AA, Collett G, Chen AF
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using propensity-score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty, stratified by peripheral artery disease diagnosis
articles.sample_size: 181,464 patients identified; 5,552 matched pairs after propensity-score matching
articles.outcomes: Surgical site infection, transfusion, anaemia, periprosthetic joint infection, wound dehiscence, revision rates, recurrent infection, mortality and lower extremity amputation at 30 days, 90 days and 3 years post-operatively
articles.take_home: Patients with peripheral artery disease who have hip replacement surgery have significantly higher rates of infection, bleeding, wound problems and need for further surgery, along with nearly four times higher risk of leg amputation within three years. Careful vascular assessment and tailored management before and after surgery are essential for these patients.

articles.title: How to conduct an effective clinical trial of cell based injection therapy for articular cartilage lesions of the knee.
articles.authors: Manzi JE, Grande D, Zaslav K
articles.study_type: Review of clinical trial design methodology
articles.population: Patients with osteochondral defects of the knee
articles.outcomes: Effectiveness of mesenchymal stem cell therapy for cartilage lesions
articles.take_home: This is a guide on how to design better clinical trials for stem cell treatments in the knee, covering important choices like what to compare against, how to deliver the cells, and what measurements to use. The paper emphasises that consistent reporting of these details across different studies is essential.

articles.title: Association of testosterone replacement therapy on medical and implant-related complications after total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Regmi A, Sami A, Baral S, Jain VK, Iyengar KP
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty, comparing those receiving testosterone replacement therapy with controls
articles.sample_size: Four retrospective matched cohort studies included
articles.outcomes: Early medical complications (pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, acute kidney injury within 3 months) and implant-related complications (periprosthetic joint infection, revision surgery, periprosthetic fracture at 12 months or longer)
articles.take_home: Men taking testosterone replacement therapy before knee replacement had similar risks of blood clots to other patients, but were more likely to develop kidney injury shortly after surgery and to need further surgery or develop implant infections later on. Testosterone replacement therapy may be a risk factor that needs considering before knee replacement.

articles.title: Design and accuracy evaluation of a new surgical instrument for determining cartilage thickness on unworn posterior femoral articular surfaces intraoperatively in kinematically aligned total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Nedopil AJ, Singh I, Hull ML
articles.population: Patients undergoing kinematically aligned total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of new surgical instrument for measuring cartilage thickness intraoperatively, with root mean square error less than 0.5 mm probe resolution
articles.take_home: A new L-shaped surgical instrument can accurately measure cartilage thickness on the unworn side of the knee during knee replacement surgery, helping surgeons restore the knee to its natural shape by comparing the worn and unworn sides.

articles.title: Clinical implications of an additional mediolateral implant option for a primary total knee system in an ethnically diverse population: 5-year interim results from a prospective, multicenter cohort study.
articles.authors: Tang Q, Violante B, McLennan-Smith R, Park KK, Charoencholvanich K
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee replacement for osteoarthritis (50% Asian, 50% Caucasian)
articles.sample_size: 148 knees in 120 patients, mean age 67.1 years, 77.5% female
articles.outcomes: Implant survival at 5 years, femoral component overhang rates, patient-reported outcomes (KOOS, KSS, EQ-VAS, EQ-5D3L), and radiographic complications
articles.take_home: A new knee implant design that better fits different ethnic anatomy had excellent survival rates at 5 years with very low complication rates and minimal overhang problems in both Asian and Caucasian patients. Patient-reported outcomes improved significantly for all participants.

articles.title: Total hip arthroplasty after hip arthrodesis: functional outcomes, and mid-term survivorship integrating the fusion technique complexity score.
articles.authors: Fahmy M, Abo-Elsoud M, Shawky MA
articles.population: Patients undergoing conversion of hip arthrodesis to total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Harris Hip Score, hip range of motion, gait, leg-length discrepancy, knee pain, radiographic assessment, implant survival
articles.take_home: Patients who had their fused hip converted to a replacement experienced significant improvement in hip function and pain, with good implant stability at mid-term follow-up of 6 years. The surgery is technically challenging but delivers substantial functional recovery despite the altered anatomy from the previous fusion.

articles.title: Total hip arthroplasty with dual-mobility components is associated with excellent clinical outcomes and low metal ion blood levels at 2 years.
articles.authors: Sandhu K, Salmon LJ, Lyons MC, Gooden BR, O'Sullivan MD
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty with dual-mobility prosthesis
articles.sample_size: 104 patients enrolled; 101 completed patient-reported outcomes; 53 had blood metal ion measurements at 2 years
articles.outcomes: Oxford Hip Score, HOOS-JR score, patient satisfaction, and whole blood cobalt, chromium and titanium levels at 2 years
articles.take_home: Patients with dual-mobility hip replacements reported excellent satisfaction and pain relief at 2 years. Metal ion levels in the blood increased slightly but remained well below levels associated with prosthetic wear problems.

articles.title: Cement Brand and Mixing Sequence Determine Vancomycin Elution from High-Dose PMMA Spacers: An in Vitro Comparative Study.
articles.authors: Hammad M, Chao CA, Bostrom MP, Carli AV
articles.population: PMMA bone cement formulations with vancomycin
articles.outcomes: Vancomycin elution over 28 days, antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, and cement porosity
articles.take_home: The brand of cement and how it is mixed (polymer-first or monomer-first) significantly affect how much vancomycin is released to fight infection. Palacos MV mixed monomer-first released the most antibiotic overall, whilst Simplex P mixed polymer-first released antibiotic fastest at the start.

articles.title: Revision Risk Following Primary Anatomic and Reverse TSA with an Exactech Equinoxe Compared with Other Devices: A U.S.-Based Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Prentice HA, Chang RN, Yian E, Navarro RA, Singh A, Chan DP, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients who had primary shoulder arthroplasty (anatomic or reverse total shoulder arthroplasty) between 2005 and 2023
articles.sample_size: 13,901 patients: 8,707 anatomic total shoulder arthroplasties, 4,374 elective reverse total shoulder arthroplasties, 820 reverse total shoulder arthroplasties for fracture
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery rates for Exactech Equinoxe devices compared with other devices
articles.take_home: Patients who received Exactech Equinoxe devices for anatomic shoulder replacement had a higher risk of needing revision surgery compared to those who received other devices. This did not apply to patients who received reverse shoulder replacements.

articles.title: Bridging the Global Implementation Gap in Immediate Weight-Bearing After Hip Fracture Surgery: The WAIT-Free Consensus for Low-Adoption Regions.
articles.authors: Mao W, Jiang J, Shi ZM, Hong CC, Turabi RY, Karim MA, et al.
articles.population: Older adults with hip fracture in low-adoption regions (China, South Asia, Southeast Asia, Middle East, Latin America, Africa)
articles.outcomes: 13 recommendations for safe implementation of immediate weight-bearing as tolerated after hip fracture surgery, organised across 4 domains: shared decision-making, mobility-based patient stratification, fall prevention, and postoperative triage
articles.take_home: An international expert group developed practical recommendations to help countries with fewer resources safely implement immediate weight-bearing after hip fracture surgery, similar to practice in North America and Europe. The recommendations can be adapted to local circumstances and include guidance on which patients are suitable and how to prevent falls during recovery.

articles.title: Vancomycin-Loaded Mesh Reduces Staphylococcal Infection in a Murine Extensor Mechanism Reconstruction Model.
articles.authors: Lin TL, Bedard NA, Karau MJ, Herren SC, Patel R, Abdel MP
articles.population: Mice with simulated extensor mechanism reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Bacterial burden on mesh and surrounding tissue, vancomycin loading capacity, mechanical properties of mesh, biofilm formation inhibition
articles.take_home: Mesh coated with vancomycin reduced bacterial infection by over 1000-fold compared to plain mesh in mice, without weakening the mesh itself. This is early laboratory work that suggests vancomycin-loaded mesh might help prevent serious infections after knee surgery, but more research is needed before it could be used in patients.

articles.title: Robotic Arthroplasty in Context: Balancing Evidence and Innovation in Joint Replacement.
articles.authors: Fraval A, Rajgopal A, Bozic KJ, Bhandari M, Parvizi J
articles.study_type: Systematic review of robotic-assisted joint replacement
articles.population: Patients undergoing joint replacement surgery
articles.outcomes: Surgical precision, component positioning, patient-reported outcomes, complication rates, implant survivorship
articles.take_home: Robotic-assisted joint replacement improves the precision of component positioning, but current evidence does not show it improves patient outcomes, reduces complications, or extends implant life. Future benefits may come from combining robotics with personalised data-driven approaches, but more rigorous research is needed.

articles.title: 'Waiting poorly' for hip and knee arthroplasty - unmet needs and lack of support while waiting for surgery : findings of the multicentre WAIT-DATA study.
articles.authors: McCann CJ, Clement ND, Gee C, Clarke J, Walmsley P, Ohly NE, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty in UK hospitals
articles.outcomes: Satisfaction with preoperative information and support across nine domains measured on five-point Likert scale; associations between patient characteristics and satisfaction levels
articles.take_home: Patients waiting for hip and knee surgery felt well informed about their condition and operation, but received poor support for weight management, general health, and mental wellbeing. People who were older, deprived, or had new health problems reported lower satisfaction, and most patients experienced worsening function and activity whilst waiting.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Following Custom Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Mannina C, Ilyas MH, Kang H, Freeman I, Sampson WT, Kwon YM
articles.study_type: Comparative observational study using institutional database
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty with at least two years follow-up
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMIS Global Physical and Mental, Physical Function scores), minimal clinically important difference achievement, 90-day complications, and two-year revision rates
articles.take_home: Custom-made knee implants performed no better than standard off-the-shelf implants for patient outcomes and pain relief, and were associated with a higher rate of needing revision surgery within two years. The theoretical advantages of custom implants did not result in any clinical benefits for patients.

articles.title: Psychological readiness is associated with long-term joint awareness after isolated anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A within-patient comparison with the contralateral healthy knee.
articles.authors: Uslu MB, Ergisi Y, Gokalp B, Comez O, Altun O, Dasar U
articles.population: Patients who underwent isolated hamstring tendon autograft anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Joint awareness using Forgotten Joint Score-12, ACL-Return to Sport after Injury scale, objective knee stability, functional scores and patient satisfaction at mean 68.5 months follow-up
articles.take_home: Reconstructed knees felt noticeably different from healthy knees even 5 years after surgery, and patients' psychological readiness to return to sport was strongly linked to how much they noticed their reconstructed knee. This suggests that addressing patients' confidence and mental readiness alongside surgery may help them achieve better long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Not all previous surgeries are the same: Procedure-specific infection risk in total knee arthroplasty patients with a history of previous knee surgery.
articles.authors: Elsheikh R, Amsler F, Brand C, Christen B, Hirschmann MT
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty with and without prior ipsilateral knee surgery
articles.sample_size: 121,692 primary total knee arthroplasties (40,535 with prior knee surgery history)
articles.outcomes: Revision for infection, all-cause revision and all-cause mortality at 2 years
articles.take_home: Patients having a new knee replacement after previous knee surgery face a higher risk of infection requiring further surgery, with some previous procedures carrying greater risk than others. Having more than two previous knee operations significantly increases infection risk.

articles.title: Arthrogenic muscle inhibition and quadriceps activation failure: Reconciling terminology and clinical perspectives across recovery phases.
articles.authors: Maffiuletti NA
articles.population: Patients with anterior cruciate ligament injury and reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Quadriceps activation failure severity and temporal patterns across recovery phases
articles.take_home: The term 'quadriceps activation failure' better describes what happens after knee ligament injury than older terminology, as it reflects multiple causes including pain, disuse and psychological factors rather than one specific mechanism. The authors propose three categories of activation failure based on timing and severity to help clinicians and researchers communicate more clearly and tailor rehabilitation accordingly.
